source.limitations: AGM presentation not re-read this session (EBITDA 2,815 and 13.9% taken from the series brief and cross-checked to the Q4 call: 2,815/20,290.43 = 13.87%). Q3 FY26 Sebi results PDF is an image scan; Q3 revenue/EBITDA taken from the press release. Who first said "16%" could not be verified. Transcript speaker attribution of 14.6%/13.9% is the CEO (Sunil D'Souza, opening remarks). The "acquisitions overpay" claim is general and uncited. Studies of takeover returns were not read. Ramu numbers are plan canonical; hurdle 10%, over-promiser and sliding-target firm are labelled one-offs. AOC-1 page: series brief says p.487, printed footer of the pdf page holding the rows is 486.

inventory.item: Management controls decisions (pricing, spend, borrowing, capital allocation) not commodity prices or monsoon
Five uses of spare cash: reinvest, acquire, dividend, buyback, repay debt
Each use passes if return beats what owners could earn elsewhere (cost of capital); Part 23 covers cost
Return on incremental capital vs average ROCE (Ramu 20.9%; rough 12.9% on FY23-26 capex 155, profit +20)
Acquisition at 8% on price paid vs 10% hurdle: worth 40 for 50, overpaid 10 (25%)
Acquirers often overpay; studies often find little gain for buyer shareholders
Buyback: stayers gain if price < ₹105 (value 100 + cash 5), lose above; zero-sum with sellers; pro-rata sell equals dividend
Buyback lifts EPS by shrinking share count
Dividends suit firms that cannot reinvest above the hurdle; ₹5 at 10% over 10 yrs = 12.97
Repay debt: saves 10%, 7.5% after 25% tax; cover 7.3x to 14.6x
Lab: ₹50 cr, four choices, ten years, sliders for reinvestment return, acquisition return, buyback price, years
Track record: what cash went into and what it earned; tenure; treatment of minorities (Part 19); candour
Ramu FY22-26 CFO 231, capex 175, FCF 56, 76% reinvested; ROE 20.2% FY25, 20.0% FY26
Guidance vs delivery: promise tracker; Ramu guided 10%, delivered 11.0/11.1/11.1
Over-promiser one-off: guided 20/18/15 delivered same
Concall: prepared remarks vs Q&A; TCPL Q4 FY26 24%/76% by words
What to listen for: volume vs price, margins, capex plans, working capital, dodged questions
TCPL Q3 FY26: India Foods revenue +19% on volume +16%; packaged tea +3% revenue, +3% volume
Q4 FY26 margin question answered without a level; follow-up: 50 to 75, 80 bps "a given"
Management claims vs audited facts: EBITDA 2,815 vs 2,791.80; adjusted EPS 17.30 vs basic 15.59
Warning signs: always next year, changing metrics, adjusted-only, blame, serial raises, silence; Parts 19/20 named

assumptions: Per share, 10 cr shares: business ₹100 (P/E 20 × EPS ₹5) held flat; spare ₹50 cr = ₹5 a share (example)
Hurdle s (stepper 0/5/10/12/15%, default 10%) = what owners earn elsewhere; cash received compounds at s
Dividend: 100 + 5(1+s)^N; Reinvest/Acquire at r: 105 + 5·r·AF, AF=((1+s)^N−1)/s (N if s=0); project valued at cost at end; profit paid out yearly
Buyback at price p for a non-tendering holder: 1000/(10−50/p); sellers get p; gains vs ₹105 net to zero; pro-rata tender equals the dividend
Sliders: reinvestment return 0-30 (20), acquisition return 0-30 (8), buyback price 60-160 step 5 (100), years 1-20 (10)
Tracker: Ramu delivery = sales growth 365→405→450→500; over-promiser guidance 20/18/15 (one-off); tolerance 0/1/2 points
